text.p: Frankie Dettori is bursting for action as the British flat racing season gets under way on Thursday and bookmakers can be forgiven for seeking shelter.
Only in their worst dreams could the odds-makers have foreseen black Saturday last September when the charismatic young master-jockey rode all seven winners at Ascot.
The cumulative odds were 25,000-1 and it cost the bookmaking fraternity an estimated 20 million pounds ($32 million).
It couldn't happen again, could it?
Bookmakers are not keen to take bets. "A man of his calibre does not sit on much dross," says William Hill spokesman David Hood.
Racing day in day out, it would be foolhardy to say the great man could never go through the card again, riding all six or seven winners in a day.
What is highly probable is that Dettori will regain the jockeys' championship he lost last year to Pat Eddery when sidelined through injury for some weeks.
With the powerful Sheikh Mohammed-string behind him and a rich pick of outside rides, 200 winners or more look well within the Italian-born jockey's grasp before the curtain comes down in November.
For the first time since Dettori came to ride in Britain, he will not have to worry about Willie Carson, the former champion who has decided reluctantly to listen to his 54-year-old body and retire.

Two memories abide strongly from last season -- Dettori punching home winner number seven at Ascot and Carson prostrate in the paddock with serious internal injuries after being kicked by a horse at Newbury.
Carson will be in the stands from now on but his friend and ex-rival Eddery will be out there battling for the old brigade, starting with the now traditional Doncaster three-day opening meeting.
However, with Irishman Kieren Fallon taking the top job at the powerful Henry Cecil stable, compatriot Eddery will be hard-pushed to land his 12th title.
The season presents a big test for Fallon, who has risen from the northern provincial circuit to land one of the top positions in the racing world.
With a history of disciplinary problems, Fallon was something of a surprise choice and he faces a searching test of temperament and talent.
Among his many top-class partners this season will be Bosra Sham, rated Europe's best filly last year after her splendid defeat of the highly-rated Halling in the Champion Stakes at Newmarket.
Cecil will be hoping Bosra Sham can help him regain the trainers' title won last year by Saeed bin Suroor for Sheikh Mohammed and his Godolphin team.

After Doncaster, thoughts move swiftly to Dubai and the World Cup on March 29 when Dettori pits his Japan Cup winner Singspiel against some tough American opposition and Helissio, the brilliant Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner.
He may warm up for that with victory on Thursday on Canyon Creek in the day's best race, while on Saturday he partners the well-fancied Grand Musica in the Lincoln Handicap.
After that, there will surely be many more and much bigger fish to fry.
